title: Option 6a: revoke a name by operator order
description: Ratified 2026-10-21. A revocation is an operator-signed record, never an agent act.
acceptance_criteria: A draft verb any agent may run emits an UNSIGNED revocation for a name plus the operator's signing command; an apply verb accepts it only if it verifies against the enrolled root.
From the revocation's time, token.py verify refuses every token for that name, expired or not, and roster.py shows the name as revoked.
Falsifier: with a valid, unexpired token, revoke the name; the token is refused. A revocation signed by any other key is refused.
No consequence attaches beyond refusing the token (PR-022 clause 4). The suite passes via goal_mode. Hand off to verifier.

notes.note: plan: build .harness/bin/revoke.py (draft/apply/revoked, own namespace harness-revocation, storage under .harness/revocations/), wire dispatch_token.verify to refuse revoked names, roster.py reports revoked status, tests in test_revoke.py plus a no-sign assertion

HANDOFF -> verifier: Built .harness/bin/revoke.py, option 6a (operator-rulings-2026-10-21.md, Decision 1).

Design: mirrors warrant.py's draft/apply split exactly.
- draft(root, name, reason="") -- any agent may run, writes UNSIGNED REV-NNN.json
  under <root>/revocations/ (not trust/), prints the ssh-keygen -Y sign command in its
  own namespace NAMESPACE="harness-revocation" (distinct from warrant/dispatch_token/
  attest namespaces). No function in revoke.py calls ssh-keygen -Y sign; pinned by
  test_revoke.py::TheModuleCannotSign (both a source-grep and an inspect.getsource scan
  of every exported callable).
- apply(root, rid) / verify_revocation -- accept a revocation only if it verifies
  against the ENROLLED root (trust/root.pub checked against trust/root.fingerprint via
  warrant.check_anchor), never against a key the file names about itself
  (test_revoke.py::OnlyTheEnrolledRootAuthorizes, including the
  "payload names its own signer as trusted" regression shape from
  test_dispatch_token.py).
- revoked_names(root)/is_revoked(root, name) -- computed on read (PR-010), re-verify
  every revocation file's signature on every call; no cache, no second registry.

Wiring:
- dispatch_token.py verify(): added a revocation check (local `import revoke as rv`
  inside verify(), before the expiry check) that raises TrustError "REVOKED NAME: ..."
  for any presented token naming a revoked agent_name, regardless of the token's own
  expiry -- matches the ruling's "refused, expired or not". ~17-line, localized diff;
  kept the import inside the function rather than the shared top-of-file import block
  since T-454 also touches this file in parallel.
- roster.py: added public revoked_report(root) (lazy `import revoke`, same pattern as
  require_warrant's lazy warrant import; never raises, returns {} if nothing has ever
  been revoked). `roster.py roster` (text) now tags a revoked name's row
  "[REVOCADO REV-NNN]" and prints a one-line disclaimer that this is a report, not a
  gate; `roster.py roster --json` adds "revoked": bool and, when true, a "revocation"
  sub-object to that name's entry. Verified by hand against a throwaway root (see
  below) and by test_revoke.py::NoConsequenceBeyondTheToken.

Acceptance criteria, point by point:
1. draft is any-agent, unsigned, prints the operator sign command; apply/verify_revocation
   accept only against the enrolled root, never a self-named key -- covered by
   TheModuleCannotSign + OnlyTheEnrolledRootAuthorizes.
2. From the revocation's time, dispatch_token.verify refuses every token for that name,
   expired or not, and roster.py shows it as revoked -- covered by TheFalsifier
   (test_revoking_the_name_refuses_a_valid_unexpired_token,
   test_revocation_refuses_an_expired_token_too) and
   NoConsequenceBeyondTheToken.test_roster_reports_the_name_as_revoked.
3. Falsifier exactly as stated: with a valid, unexpired token, revoke the name, the
   token is refused (test_revoking_the_name_refuses_a_valid_unexpired_token); a
   revocation signed by any other key is refused
   (test_a_revocation_signed_by_any_other_key_is_refused, which also re-confirms the
   original token still verifies because the forged revocation never took effect).
4. No consequence beyond refusing the token: the payload itself carries a
   NOT_A_CONSEQUENCE string (test_revocation_carries_no_consequence_marker); PUBLIC_API
   scanned for threshold/gate/weight/burden/permission parameters
   (test_no_exported_callable_takes_a_threshold_gate_weight_burden_or_permission),
   mirroring test_roster.py's own guard. Revoking one name does not refuse another
   (test_revoking_one_name_does_not_refuse_another).

Replay commands (all green):
  python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_revoke.py .harness/tests/test_dispatch_token.py .harness/tests/test_roster.py .harness/tests/test_warrant.py -q
    -> 150 passed in 13.51s
  python3 .harness/bin/goal_mode.py run --cmd "python3 -m pytest .harness/tests -q"
    -> GOAL REACHED: succeeded on iteration 1/3 (112.31s)

Manually exercised the CLI end to end (throwaway root in tempfile.TemporaryDirectory,
no live state touched -- confirmed `.harness/revocations` does not exist on the live
tree and `git status --porcelain .harness/` shows no stray revocation files):
  revoke.py draft --name worker-a --reason "stolen key"  -> unsigned REV-001.json + sign command
  <operator signs>
  revoke.py apply --revocation REV-001                   -> {"applied": true, ...}
  roster.py --root <tmp> roster                           -> worker-a row tagged "[REVOCADO REV-001]"
  roster.py --root <tmp> roster --json                     -> names.worker-a.revoked == true

No signing happened anywhere in the live tree or against the operator's real
~/.ssh/harness_root; both the manual exercise and every test use a throwaway root key
generated inside tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(), same shape as test_warrant.py and
test_dispatch_token.py.
